verified_contracts: Every indexed selector in world.rs maps to an explicit scenario; four pre-indexed emitters are cross-checked against their literal Rust source. Unexpected selector/dispatcher shapes fail planning.

Expected identities are carried in the actual workflow matrix, revalidated on export/summarize, and compared to exactly one terminal verdict. Capture-only, different slices/IDs, duplicates and incomplete batches cannot satisfy those identities.

Reference default batch (0,15) matches e2e_row_batch.rs. indexed_verdict.rs buffers its own row verdict, rewrites optimistic outcomes after cleanup failures and emits missing failure evidence on interrupted reporters.

Existing FAIL/MISSING status policy is retained: extract returns failure from node boot result/exit and workflow summary separately requires successful shard jobs. This does not claim new completeness checks for groups/basic/spells/game-platform.

All three S3B PASS_EVIDENCE strings match terminal Rust body markers. The wrapper retains --ignored --exact --nocapture selection, requires successful one-test libtest summary, selected-case line and mode-specific terminal marker, and preserves child failure through pipefail.

New S3B regression tests execute the actual caller tail/cleanup/mode selection with only the child test process substituted; they cover real positive shapes, zero/wrong/duplicate/ignored/incomplete evidence and failed children.

Follow-up root fixture repair: run_aggregate now supplies every actual planned indexed scenario while retaining generic identities only for non-indexed groups. Both actual PR and MQ aggregate shell bodies reject missing/wrong/capture-only row evidence. Existing independent build/platform/shard/World/default-image gates and MISSING informational policy remain asserted. Using the plan for valid fixture identities is paired with deliberate incomplete/wrong-status mutations, not an oracle replacing the gate result.

observed_checks.scope: Actual PR and MQ aggregate scripts with positive and all existing/new negative subcases; full heavy-gate module run is root-owned.

limits: Review covered the four changed diffs and targeted caller/consumer contracts, not complete semantic review of every caller file.
